places.name: London
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)

places.name: Worcester and County Lunatic Asylum, Powick
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Conducted the attendants’ band weekly for five years, writing quadrilles and polkas for its odd instrumentation.

places.name: Brompton Oratory, London
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Married Alice Roberts; they tried and failed to establish themselves in London, where their daughter Carice was born.

places.name: Three Choirs Festival, Worcester
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Conducted the first performance of the overture Froissart, his first major work, for the festival committee.

places.name: Great Malvern (Forli, then Craeg Lea)
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Settled in Alice’s old home town in 1891; moved to Craeg Lea in 1899, keeping Birchwood as a second home.

places.name: St James’s Hall, London
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)

places.name: Birmingham Town Hall
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)

places.name: Liverpool
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)

places.name: Covent Garden, London
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: A three-day festival of his works, an honour never before given to an English composer.

places.name: Plâs Gwyn, Hampton Park Road, Hereford
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Large house above the River Wye; he wrote much of his best music here. Now flats called Elgar Court.

places.name: Buckingham Palace, London
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Knighted at the Palace; the next month the family moved to Hereford.

places.name: Free Trade Hall, Manchester
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: The First Symphony premiered under Hans Richter and the Hallé; it was a national and international triumph.

places.name: London (Royal Philharmonic Society)

places.name: Queen’s Hall, London
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Second Symphony premiered at the London Musical Festival under the composer; the reception was cooler than for the First.

places.name: Severn House, 42 Netherhall Gardens, Hampstead
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: A Norman Shaw mansion with a music room, where he wrote The Music Makers and Falstaff; since demolished.

places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Rented countryside house where he recovered his strength and wrote the Violin Sonata, Piano Quintet and String Quartet.

sources.title: The Elgar Trail: A Short Illustrated Tour of Elgar’s Houses (The Elgar Society)

places.name: Wigmore Hall, London
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: The String Quartet and Piano Quintet premiered, written at Brinkwells and warmly received.

places.name: London Symphony Orchestra season opener

places.what: The Cello Concerto had a disastrous premiere, for lack of rehearsal time; Elgar later recorded it twice.

places.name: Napleton Grange, Kempsey
places.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (today United Kingdom)
places.what: Returned to Worcestershire after Alice’s death; he arranged Bach and Handel and wrote the Empire March for 1924.

places.what: Bought a house with a view of the cathedral; in January 1934 he followed an Abbey Road session by telephone.
